discussion.title: BIP460: CISA for Taproot Key Path Spends

options.name: BIP 460
options.gloss: Cross input signature aggregation for taproot key path spends

claims.quote: It introduces witness version 2, which enables Taproot-style key path spending where inputs can aggregate their signatures within a transaction.
claims.text: The BIP introduces witness version 2 enabling Taproot-style key path spends with in-transaction signature aggregation.

claims.quote: Each input chooses between half-aggregation, full-aggregation, or an explicit opt-out via a marker byte in its witness and the signature message commits to that choice.
claims.text: Each input selects half-aggregation, full-aggregation, or opt-out via a witness marker byte committed to in the signature message.

claims.quote: this version incorporates feedback from vostrnad, most notably a rewritten rationale for excluding script path aggregation, describing the conflict with the `OP_SUCCESS` upgrade mechanism.
claims.text: Script path aggregation is excluded because it conflicts with the OP_SUCCESS upgrade mechanism.

claims.quote: The test vectors are generated with Python code that builds on the reference implementations of BIP458 and BIP459, and the latest master of secp256k1lab is vendored with the BIP
claims.text: Test vectors are generated from BIP458/459 reference implementations with secp256k1lab vendored in.

claims.quote: Since witness versions are a scarce resource and not assigning them sequential would be kind of confusing, it seems whatever soft fork goes in next that requires a new witness version should get the n
claims.text: Witness versions are scarce, so the next soft fork needing one should take the next available number.

claims.quote: Maybe we'll want to move to a more generic language for the version instead of prescribing it explicitly until activation comes close.
claims.text: Specs could use generic version language until activation nears.

claims.quote: On the other hand, maybe making it explicit and avoiding collisions makes sense for tests on Bitcoin Inquisition etc.
claims.text: Explicit, collision-free version assignment may help testing on Bitcoin Inquisition.

claims.quote: Either way, it can't be avoided that there is a chance a "final" BIP might need a change in this regard at some point when it actually gets activated.
claims.text: A finalized BIP may still need a witness version change at activation time.

claims.quote: This completes the CISA BIP triplet with half-agg (458) and full-agg (459) and should get BIP number 460
claims.text: This proposal completes the CISA BIP set alongside half-agg (458) and full-agg (459) and should be assigned BIP 460.

claims.quote: but I will wait for the editor confirmation again :)
claims.text: The author will wait for BIP editor confirmation before finalizing the number.

claims.quote: I don't think this requires BIP-342, BIP-341 didn't require it either.
claims.text: The proposal should not list BIP-342 as a requirement, since BIP-341 did not require it.

claims.quote: saying that the 32-byte witness program is a public key introduces a tiny bit of ambiguity as to whether the following validation rules apply when the witness program isn't a valid public key
claims.text: Calling the 32-byte witness program a public key creates ambiguity about whether the validation rules apply when it is not a valid public key.

claims.quote: Since addresses are a standard that exists outside of consensus rules, I'd mention them in a different section.
claims.text: Addresses are outside consensus rules, so they belong in a separate section.

claims.quote: that way you'd have one less thing to worry about should you ever change it to SegWit v3 or something else
claims.text: Omitting address details reduces maintenance if the witness version changes later.

claims.quote: the specification section in a consensus change BIP should be highly focused on the validation rules, so this feels out of place anyway
claims.text: A consensus-change BIP's specification section should focus on validation rules, so this text doesn't belong there.

claims.quote: This feels like too much text for describing the simple fact that script path validation rules are unchanged between SegWit v1 and v2.
claims.text: The section is overly verbose for stating that script path validation rules are unchanged between v1 and v2.

claims.quote: I think it would be great to base the whole specification on the fact that validation of v2 spends is identical to v1 except for a concrete list of differences
claims.text: The whole spec should be framed as v1 validation plus a concrete list of differences.

claims.quote: You could then remove or simplify other text that just reiterates this, like the annex handling section or the invalid empty witness point below.
claims.text: Redundant text such as annex handling and the empty witness point could then be removed or simplified.

claims.quote: It seems a bit inconsistent to have sections named Rationale (which describes rationale inline) and Footnotes (which describes rationale as footnotes).
claims.text: Having separate Rationale and Footnotes sections is inconsistent since both present rationale in different forms.

claims.quote: As an example, BIP-341 only has a Rationale section where all points are footnotes, and that way they can be referenced inline from places where the rationale needs explaining.
claims.text: BIP-341's approach of a single Rationale section with footnote points allows inline referencing where explanation is needed.

claims.quote: The use cases motivating this BIP, collaborative transactions and consolidations, also typically spend simple key path inputs.
claims.text: Suggests rewording to state that the BIP's motivating use cases (collaborative transactions and consolidations) typically spend simple key path inputs.

claims.quote: Using the same HD derivation paths for both SegWit v1 and v2 seems like a bad idea for multiple reasons.
claims.text: Reusing identical HD derivation paths across SegWit v1 and v2 is a bad idea.

claims.quote: I think the whole Taproot compatibility section can be removed, pointing out that you can have v1 and v2 inputs in the same transaction feels very much redundant.
claims.text: The Taproot compatibility section is redundant and should be removed.

claims.quote: But here it says it would have its own leaf version, which is not necessary if it's added in the same soft fork.
claims.text: The document is inconsistent: assigning script path aggregation its own leaf version is unnecessary if it ships in the same soft fork.

claims.quote: I would also expect that whatever gets deployed first would get to use the next version and other proposals would shift.
claims.text: Whichever proposal deploys first should claim the next witness version, with others shifting.

claims.quote: I guess you could write “version 2 (or the next unencumbered version available when this proposal is deployed)” or similar to be abundantly clear.
claims.text: The BIP could phrase the version as 'version 2 or the next unencumbered version available' for clarity.

claims.quote: At least one of the authors of BIP 360 was keen on using version 3 anyway, because he wanted quantum-**r**esistant addresses to start with bc1**r**.
claims.text: A BIP 360 author prefers version 3 so quantum-resistant addresses start with bc1r.

claims.quote: Removed
claims.text: The author states the item in question has been removed.

claims.quote: Changed to witness program, matching BIP 341 as suggested.
claims.text: The author updated the terminology to "witness program" to match BIP 341, per the reviewer's suggestion.

claims.quote: Right, BIP 350 already covers this. Removed.
claims.text: Author agrees the content is already covered by BIP 350 and has removed it.

claims.quote: the section now follows the BIP 342 approach of stating the modifications to the BIP 341 rules, and the redundant parts like the annex section and the empty witness rule are removed
claims.text: The section was rewritten to state only modifications to BIP 341 rules, per BIP 342's style, dropping redundant annex and empty-witness text.

claims.quote: I was under the impression that BIPs generally are more explicit when it comes to parts that are unchanged but I found plenty of counter examples and I prefer less text as well.
claims.text: The author's assumption that BIPs restate unchanged parts explicitly was contradicted by counterexamples, and he prefers less text.

claims.quote: It is consistent with, for example, BIP340 and BIP458 (where I didn't come up with the initial structure). Both mix prose rationale and a separate footnotes section.
claims.text: The current structure matches precedent in BIP340 and BIP458, which both mix prose rationale with a separate footnotes section.

claims.quote: I think such a split can help with readability by keeping the parts that are deeper in the weeds in the footnotes.
claims.text: Splitting deeper technical details into footnotes improves readability.

claims.quote: Reworded to 'use simple key path spends'.
claims.text: The author changed the wording to 'use simple key path spends'.

claims.quote: Good catch, changed the wording to 'with its own upgrade semantics'.
claims.text: Author accepted the reviewer's point and reworded the text to 'with its own upgrade semantics'.

claims.quote: Addressed inline comments from @vostrnad , thanks again for the extensive review!
claims.text: The author addressed vostrnad's inline review comments.

claims.quote: I am still open to consider adding this if reviewers can envision possible use cases or are just generally of the opinion we should offer as much flexibility as possible
claims.text: The author remains open to adding the feature if reviewers can identify use cases or favor maximum flexibility.

claims.quote: Also added the assigned number and made changes in response the recent renaming of BIP459.
claims.text: The BIP now includes its assigned number and reflects the BIP459 renaming.

claims.quote: I have something like this in the deployment section already, so I didn't make any further change in this regard.
claims.text: No change was made regarding version wording because the deployment section already covers it.

claims.quote: Marker values are disjoint from valid sighash values, so this resolves the 65-byte ambiguity that the opt-out marker existed to resolve.
claims.text: Moving markers to the sighash byte position resolves the 65-byte ambiguity without a separate opt-out marker.

claims.quote: Aggregated inputs are otherwise unchanged and their messages still commit to the mode, so aggregation remains consensual.
claims.text: Aggregation remains consensual because messages still commit to the mode.

claims.quote: if external factors like PQ migration drive part of the adoption of the output type, opted-out spends may be less of an exception than I thought
claims.text: PQ migration driving adoption means opted-out spends may be common rather than exceptional.

claims.quote: With this change a wallet that never aggregates spends witness v2 outputs with its existing Taproot signing logic, no new sighash code path, no new witness logic.
claims.text: Non-aggregating wallets could spend witness v2 outputs with existing Taproot signing logic.

claims.quote: A CISA-enabled witness v2 becomes a strict superset of a plain "P2TRv2" with BIP 341 semantics.
claims.text: CISA-enabled witness v2 becomes a strict superset of a plain P2TRv2.

claims.quote: Opted-out spends are byte-identical to BIP 341 key path spends: same witness, same message, same signing code, making initial adoption easier
claims.text: Byte-identical opted-out spends make initial adoption easier.

claims.quote: One byte saved per opted-out input.
claims.text: The change saves one byte per opted-out input.

claims.quote: Cross-version replay protection between v1 and v2 now rests on the scriptPubKey commitment in SigMsg instead of a separate sighash epoch.
claims.text: Con: cross-version replay protection now relies on the scriptPubKey commitment rather than a sighash epoch.

claims.quote: The marker sits at the end of the element, unlike other tags in the taproot family, and its values cannot become sighash types in a future witness version that inherits this grammar.
claims.text: Con: trailing marker placement is unusual and burns potential future sighash values.

claims.quote: By now I believe that this is an improvement even if there is no combination with a PQ P2TRv2 proposal
claims.text: The revision is an improvement independent of any PQ P2TRv2 combination.

claims.quote: Nit: It's unusual to document the _last_ element of an object's encoding _first._
claims.text: Documenting the marker (last byte) first in the encoding spec is unconventional.

claims.quote: I think there would still be a difference w/r/t the witness program version, and perhaps some implementations naively assume the witness version during message hashing.
claims.text: Opted-out spends aren't fully identical to BIP341 since the witness version differs and may be assumed during message hashing.

claims.quote: Perhaps that one byte is still worth mentioning?
claims.text: The one-byte witness version change should still be mentioned in the spec.

claims.quote: Crazy idea, but could you flip this logic on its head, and swap the signature message functions of the "opted out" and "half-agg" signatures?
claims.text: Proposes swapping the sighash functions so the default lazy path is half-aggregatable and opt-out requires explicit work.

claims.quote: users who upgrade to CISA addresses would automatically gain the benefits of half-aggregation without doing any work aside from changing the witness version
claims.text: Under the swapped design, upgraders get half-agg benefits automatically via third-party aggregation.

claims.quote: This has a security drawback though, for users who depend on adaptor signatures. They'd need to update their systems, using stock BIP341 signatures would subject their signatures to half-aggregation,
claims.text: The swapped design risks accidental half-aggregation of adaptor signatures, requiring users to update systems.

claims.quote: It also places an expected burden of doing half-agg work on the rest of the network, when really it should be the spender's wallet software.
claims.text: The swapped design shifts aggregation burden onto the network instead of the spender's wallet.

claims.quote: I don't know of any limits applying in this situation. The 520b stack element size limit doesn't apply. The 10000 byte script size limit doesn't apply.
claims.text: Known script/stack size limits don't apply to the variable-size half-agg signature.

claims.quote: This approach would have the added bonus that all the keyspend witness elements will become fixed-size (33 bytes for half-agg placeholders, 65 bytes for half-agg finals, i think), making parsing a lit
claims.text: Distributing nonce components across inputs would yield fixed-size witness elements and easier parsing.

claims.quote: But on the replay concern: the witness version is in the message through the committed scriptPubKey, so an implementation that wrongly assumes v1 there should produce an invalid signature and replayin
claims.text: Replay is prevented because the scriptPubKey commitment includes the witness version, making wrong-version signatures invalid.

claims.quote: the deal breaker IMO would be witness maleability. If third parties could fold plain signatures in the mempool, the same transaction would validly exist in multiple witness encodings.
claims.text: Swapping the message functions would allow third parties to fold plain signatures, causing witness malleability.

claims.quote: Wtxids would change in flight and that would degrade a lot of stuff that we are doing in P2P and local optimization, things like tx relay, compact blocks and caching.
claims.text: Wtxid changes in flight would degrade tx relay, compact blocks, and caching.

claims.quote: L2 protocols like Lightning would likely also have a lot of work to do to adapt to this and there would likely be security issues from this as well.
claims.text: L2 protocols like Lightning would need major adaptation and may face security issues from that change.

claims.quote: Correct, nothing should bind this below the transaction weight limits afaik.
claims.text: No limit other than transaction weight limits binds the witness size here.

claims.quote: I worked through this encoding and it indeed makes every element fixed-size, and distributes the witness weight of the aggregate almost evenly across the group.
claims.text: Distributing nonce components across inputs makes elements fixed-size and spreads witness weight evenly.

claims.quote: That nicely dissolves the question of who pays for the final input's extra weight.
claims.text: The distributed encoding resolves the question of who pays for the final input's extra weight.

claims.quote: these members need no marker at all anymore since their lengths are disjoint from everything else, and full-agg members can shrink to an empty witness element because of that
claims.text: Disjoint lengths remove the need for markers and allow full-agg members to use an empty witness element.

claims.quote: The marker overhead can be reduced to one byte per group which is on the final input only. And this also means of course we save one weight unit per member (-1 for the last).
claims.text: Marker overhead drops to one byte per group, saving a weight unit per member.

claims.quote: after spending some more time with it and making some minor improvements to the text compared to the draft versions linked above
claims.text: The pushed version includes minor textual improvements over the earlier linked drafts.

claims.quote: Updated due to the change in the tagged hashes in BIP458 and BIP459.
claims.text: The author updated the PR to reflect changes to the tagged hashes in BIP458 and BIP459.

questions.text: Should this BIP keep witness version 2 despite colliding with BIP360, or should the editors assign a different version?
Should the stated validation rules apply when the 32-byte witness program is not a valid x-coordinate of a curve point?
What is the quoted specification text actually supposed to mean?
Should script path aggregation require a separate leaf version, or only if deployed in a later soft fork?
Does anyone see downsides to making opted-out inputs plain BIP 341 key path spends that I have missed?
Could half-agg groups hit any witness size limit that caps the number of aggregated signatures n?
Why attach a growing variable-size half-agg signature to one input instead of distributing nonce components across each input's witness?

_prototype_note: Machine extraction by claude-opus-5, not reviewed by a human. A single-proposal thread, so there is no option axis to pivot on.
